semantic_purpose: A self-contained composition intended to be independently reusable or distributable.
common_use_cases: Blog post; news story; forum post; product card with standalone identity; user comment.
improvement_over_generic: Exposes independence as native document meaning instead of a private class convention.
accessibility_effect: May create an article structure; headings help users identify the unit.
seo_effect: Helps systems distinguish a standalone content unit; an isolated ranking boost is not documented.
constraints: Use only when the content makes sense independently; nested articles should relate to the containing article.

semantic_purpose: A generic thematic section of a document or application, usually identified by a heading.
common_use_cases: Chapters; grouped service details; report sections; tabbed thematic panels.
improvement_over_generic: Makes thematic grouping explicit in the HTML vocabulary.
accessibility_effect: A named section may expose a region; excessive unnamed sections create noise.
seo_effect: Supports coherent content structure, but is not a keyword-weighting switch or confirmed ranking factor.
constraints: Use article, nav, aside, or address when their narrower meaning applies; normally include a heading.

semantic_purpose: A section whose purpose is major navigation.
common_use_cases: Primary menu; breadcrumbs container; table of contents; pagination or major index.
improvement_over_generic: Creates native navigation meaning and normally an accessibility landmark.
accessibility_effect: Screen-reader users may jump to it; multiple nav landmarks need distinct names.
seo_effect: Clarifies navigational blocks and link context; no confirmed special PageRank weighting follows merely from the tag.
constraints: Not every link group belongs in nav. Label repeated navigation landmarks.

semantic_purpose: Content tangentially related to its surrounding content.
common_use_cases: Sidebar; related resources; pull quote; author note; advertising.
improvement_over_generic: Expresses complementary rather than primary relevance.
accessibility_effect: Usually maps to a complementary landmark when context permits; repeated landmarks need names.
seo_effect: May help separate supplementary material from main content; ranking effects are not documented.
constraints: Content must remain related yet non-essential to the surrounding flow.

semantic_purpose: Introductory or navigational aids for a page or section.
common_use_cases: Site masthead; article title/byline group; section introduction.
improvement_over_generic: Meaning depends on its nearest sectioning context and is not limited to the page top.
accessibility_effect: A body-level header may map to banner; nested headers generally do not.
seo_effect: Clarifies introductions and heading context; no isolated ranking benefit is confirmed.
constraints: May appear several times; do not nest within header or footer, and observe content-model restrictions.

semantic_purpose: Footer information for its nearest sectioning ancestor or the page.
common_use_cases: Author details; copyright; related links; revision data.
improvement_over_generic: Associates closing metadata with the correct page or section.
accessibility_effect: A body-level footer may map to contentinfo; nested footers generally do not.
seo_effect: Helps classify supporting metadata; no isolated ranking benefit is confirmed.
constraints: May appear more than once; its meaning is scoped to the nearest sectioning ancestor.

semantic_purpose: The dominant content of the document body, excluding repeated site-wide material.
common_use_cases: Primary article; product detail; service page content; application workspace.
improvement_over_generic: Creates a native main landmark without role="main".
accessibility_effect: Provides a direct destination for landmark navigation and skip links.
seo_effect: Separates unique page content from repeated chrome; direct rank improvement is not documented.
constraints: Normally one visible main per document; do not nest in article, aside, footer, header, or nav.

semantic_purpose: A part of a document containing controls or content for performing a search or filtering operation.
common_use_cases: Site search; product filter controls; on-page search.
improvement_over_generic: Provides native search landmark semantics without an ARIA role.
accessibility_effect: Exposes a search landmark where supported.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect established; improves native meaning and accessibility.
constraints: Use for search/filter functionality, not a section merely discussing search.

semantic_purpose: Contact information for the nearest article or document body.
common_use_cases: Author email; organization contact link; page-owner contact details.
improvement_over_generic: Associates contact data with its responsible author or organization.
accessibility_effect: Supplies semantic contact context but does not replace accessible labels or structured data.
seo_effect: May clarify authorship/contact context; does not replace Organization/Person structured data.
constraints: Do not use for arbitrary postal addresses unrelated to the author/owner.

semantic_purpose: Self-contained content referenced as a unit, optionally with a caption.
common_use_cases: Image; diagram; chart; code listing; quotation; data table.
improvement_over_generic: Groups the asset and its caption as one semantic unit.
accessibility_effect: Provides structural association; image alt text remains independently required when applicable.
seo_effect: Improves media-context organization; figure alone does not guarantee image-search gains.
constraints: Figcaption, when present, must be the first or last child.

semantic_purpose: Caption or legend for its parent figure.
common_use_cases: Chart caption; image explanation; code-sample label.
improvement_over_generic: Creates a native relationship to the entire figure.
accessibility_effect: Adds visible context but is not a substitute for image alternative text.
seo_effect: Provides nearby descriptive context that search systems may process; no ranking guarantee.
constraints: Must be inside figure and should be first or last child.

semantic_purpose: Native disclosure widget whose additional content may be expanded or collapsed.
common_use_cases: FAQ answer; specifications; optional explanation; disclosure panel.
improvement_over_generic: Supplies built-in state, activation, and keyboard behavior with less custom scripting.
accessibility_effect: Native disclosure semantics and focus behavior reduce custom-widget failure risk.
seo_effect: Collapsed content remains in the DOM; indexing or ranking treatment is not guaranteed by the element.
constraints: Use summary as the label; test browser and assistive-technology behavior.

semantic_purpose: Visible label and activation control for a parent details element.
common_use_cases: FAQ question; disclosure title.
improvement_over_generic: Creates the native interactive label for details.
accessibility_effect: Keyboard-operable control semantics are supplied by the browser.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect established.
constraints: Must be the first summary child of details to act as its summary.

semantic_purpose: A dialog box or other interactive component presented over or apart from the page flow.
common_use_cases: Modal confirmation; settings panel; non-modal dialog.
improvement_over_generic: Native dialog API supports modal display and focus-management primitives.
accessibility_effect: Correct use improves focus containment and dialog announcement; accessible naming remains required.
seo_effect: No direct SEO benefit; hidden modal content should not carry essential primary-page information.
constraints: Supply an accessible name; use showModal() for modal behavior; do not misuse for ordinary layout.

semantic_purpose: Headings that identify sections and communicate rank.
common_use_cases: Page title; major section; nested subsection.
improvement_over_generic: Creates a programmatic heading hierarchy independent of visual styling.
accessibility_effect: Screen-reader users navigate and scan by headings.
seo_effect: Google documents headings as useful signals for understanding page structure and title-link context, but mechanical level rules do not guarantee rank.
constraints: Choose levels by hierarchy, not font size; do not leave headings empty.

semantic_purpose: A paragraph of text.
common_use_cases: Explanatory prose; answer text; description.
generic_or_legacy_pattern: div with text and line breaks
improvement_over_generic: Exposes paragraph boundaries rather than visual spacing only.
accessibility_effect: Supports coherent reading units.
seo_effect: No independent ranking effect; correct text structure improves parsing and maintenance.
constraints: Do not place flow-content blocks inside p.

semantic_purpose: An unordered list of items.
common_use_cases: Feature list; related resources; non-sequential steps.
generic_or_legacy_pattern: div rows with bullets added by CSS
improvement_over_generic: Exposes list membership and item count.
accessibility_effect: Screen readers announce list structure.
seo_effect: No direct ranking boost; makes enumerated content explicit.
constraints: Children are li elements, apart from script-supporting elements.

semantic_purpose: An ordered list whose sequence matters.
common_use_cases: Instructions; rankings; legal steps; chronology.
improvement_over_generic: Exposes order and list-item relationships.
accessibility_effect: Screen readers announce ordered-list structure and count.
seo_effect: No direct ranking boost; clarifies procedural or ranked relationships.
constraints: Use reversed, start, and value only when their numeric meaning is intended.

semantic_purpose: An association list made of term/name groups and their descriptions/values.
common_use_cases: Glossary; metadata; specifications; question-answer pairs where term-description semantics fit.
improvement_over_generic: Creates explicit term-description relationships.
accessibility_effect: Assistive support varies in announcement detail but relationships remain native HTML.
seo_effect: No direct ranking effect; improves machine-readable association.
constraints: Use dt and dd groups; not merely for visual indentation.

semantic_purpose: A section quoted from another source.
common_use_cases: Long testimonial excerpt; cited passage.
improvement_over_generic: Marks quotation semantics without relying on indentation.
accessibility_effect: Conveys quoted-block meaning.
seo_effect: No direct rank effect; cite attribute is not normally displayed and does not replace a visible source link.
constraints: Use cite attribute only for a source URL; add visible attribution separately.

semantic_purpose: A short inline quotation.
common_use_cases: Quoted phrase inside a sentence.
improvement_over_generic: Marks the phrase as quoted while user agents handle punctuation.
accessibility_effect: Conveys inline quotation semantics.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect.
constraints: Do not add quotation marks solely through text when q supplies them; cite may hold a source URL.

semantic_purpose: The title of a creative work.
common_use_cases: Book; article; film; research paper title.
improvement_over_generic: Identifies a work title rather than merely styling text.
accessibility_effect: Conveys work-title meaning; default italics are presentation only.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect.
constraints: Not intended for a person name under the HTML standard.

semantic_purpose: Stress emphasis that changes sentence meaning.
common_use_cases: Contrastive stress; verbal emphasis.
improvement_over_generic: Encodes stress rather than appearance.
accessibility_effect: May alter spoken emphasis depending on assistive technology.
seo_effect: No proven keyword-weighting benefit.
constraints: Use CSS for italics without stress; nesting increases emphasis level.

semantic_purpose: Strong importance, seriousness, or urgency.
common_use_cases: Warning; critical instruction; important phrase.
improvement_over_generic: Encodes importance rather than appearance.
accessibility_effect: May expose importance, though screen-reader voicing varies.
seo_effect: No proven keyword-weighting benefit.
constraints: Use b or CSS when only visual offset is intended.

semantic_purpose: Text marked as relevant in the current context.
common_use_cases: Search-result match; referenced passage; review highlight.
improvement_over_generic: Encodes contextual relevance rather than yellow background.
accessibility_effect: Color alone must not be the sole cue; announcement support varies.
seo_effect: No direct ranking effect; it is not an SEO keyword-highlighting mechanism.
constraints: Do not use merely for decorative highlighting or general importance.

semantic_purpose: A machine-readable date, time, time-zone offset, or duration.
common_use_cases: Publication date; event time; opening duration.
improvement_over_generic: The datetime attribute disambiguates human date formats.
accessibility_effect: Supports unambiguous programmatic interpretation.
seo_effect: May help systems parse dates, but does not replace structured data required for search features.
constraints: datetime must use a valid HTML date/time or duration syntax.

semantic_purpose: Human-readable content paired with a machine-readable value.
common_use_cases: Product identifier; internal code; machine value for a label.
improvement_over_generic: Uses a standard value attribute for machine-readable equivalence.
accessibility_effect: Limited direct accessibility effect; visible label remains necessary.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect; does not replace structured data vocabulary.
constraints: Use time instead when the value is a date or time.

semantic_purpose: An abbreviation or acronym, optionally with its expansion.
common_use_cases: Technical acronym; shortened organization name.
improvement_over_generic: Marks abbreviated text and may provide its expansion.
accessibility_effect: Title-only expansions are not reliably accessible; provide visible expansion when important.
seo_effect: May clarify language processing, but no direct ranking boost is documented.
constraints: Do not rely solely on title for essential information.

semantic_purpose: The defining instance of a term.
common_use_cases: Glossary definition; first formal definition.
improvement_over_generic: Identifies where a term is being defined.
accessibility_effect: Provides semantic definition context.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect established.
constraints: The nearest paragraph, dt/dd group, or section should contain the definition.

semantic_purpose: A fragment of computer code.
common_use_cases: HTML tag; command; function name.
improvement_over_generic: Identifies code independent of font choice.
accessibility_effect: Screen readers may not announce punctuation adequately; explanatory prose may still be needed.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect.
constraints: Use pre with code for preformatted blocks.

semantic_purpose: An actionable button.
common_use_cases: Submit; expand; open dialog; run command.
generic_or_legacy_pattern: div or span with click handler
improvement_over_generic: Provides keyboard activation, focusability, role, disabled state, and form behavior natively.
accessibility_effect: Major accessibility gain over scripted generic containers.
seo_effect: No direct ranking effect; improves usable interaction and crawl-independent page quality.
constraints: Set type explicitly in forms; give an accessible name.

semantic_purpose: A hyperlink to a URL or document location.
common_use_cases: Internal link; external citation; email or telephone link.
improvement_over_generic: Creates native link semantics, focus behavior, URL handling, and crawlable relationships when href is present.
accessibility_effect: Keyboard and screen-reader link navigation work natively.
seo_effect: Google explicitly uses crawlable links and anchor text to discover pages and understand linked content.
constraints: Use href for hyperlinks; buttons are for actions that do not navigate.

semantic_purpose: A caption associated with a form control.
common_use_cases: Input name; checkbox label; select label.
improvement_over_generic: Creates a programmatic name relationship and a larger activation target.
accessibility_effect: Essential for control identification and speech/assistive input.
seo_effect: No direct SEO effect.
constraints: Associate with for/id or by nesting; placeholder is not a label replacement.

semantic_purpose: Data with relationships across rows and columns.
common_use_cases: Pricing matrix; specifications; comparison; report data.
improvement_over_generic: Creates native row, column, header, caption, and cell relationships.
accessibility_effect: Correct th/scope/caption markup supports table navigation and comprehension.
seo_effect: May clarify data relationships; no rich-result eligibility follows from table markup alone.
constraints: Do not use for page layout. Use caption and header cells where needed.

semantic_purpose: Groups interactive controls into a single submittable unit tied to one user action.
common_use_cases: Search boxes, sign-up and login forms, checkout flows, contact forms, on-page filters.
generic_or_legacy_pattern: div wrapper with a JS click handler simulating submission
improvement_over_generic: Provides native submission, keyboard Enter-to-submit, and built-in validation; only exposes a form or search landmark role when it has an accessible name.
accessibility_effect: Exposed as a form (or search) landmark to assistive tech only when labelled with aria-label or aria-labelledby; unlabelled forms are not distinguishable from each other in landmark navigation.
seo_effect: No direct ranking effect; a labelled form clarifies page purpose (e.g. distinguishing a search form from a contact form) for automated interpretation.
constraints: Needs an accessible name to register as a landmark (SEM-006); avoid nesting one form inside another.

semantic_purpose: Embeds an image and, through the alt attribute, supplies a text alternative that stands in for the image's meaning.
common_use_cases: Product photography, illustrative diagrams and charts, logos, purely decorative graphics (alt="").
generic_or_legacy_pattern: CSS background-image applied to a div
improvement_over_generic: alt text is exposed to screen readers and image-search crawlers; a CSS background-image carries no accessible name or indexable text alternative.
accessibility_effect: alt is the image's accessible name; an empty alt="" correctly hides purely decorative images from assistive technology instead of announcing a meaningless filename.
seo_effect: alt text is a confirmed input to Google Image Search relevance and a documented accessibility requirement; it is not established as a general web-ranking factor on its own.
constraints: Always set alt (empty string for decorative images); do not keyword-stuff alt text.

semantic_purpose: Represents one item within an ordered, unordered, or menu list.
common_use_cases: Navigation links, numbered steps, product feature lists, search result entries.
generic_or_legacy_pattern: div per row inside a div acting as a fake list
improvement_over_generic: Only valid as a child of ul, ol, or menu, so the browser exposes real list semantics (item count and position) that a div-per-row structure cannot.
accessibility_effect: Announced by screen readers with position and set size (for example "item 2 of 5") only when correctly nested inside ul or ol.
seo_effect: No independent ranking effect; correctly marked-up list items make enumerable content (steps, features) easier for automated systems to extract for rich results.
constraints: Must be a direct child of ul, ol, or menu; not valid on its own.

semantic_purpose: Preserves whitespace and line breaks exactly as authored, for content where formatting is part of the meaning.
common_use_cases: Code snippets (paired with code), ASCII art, terminal or console output.
generic_or_legacy_pattern: div styled with white-space:pre-wrap and manual br tags
improvement_over_generic: Whitespace preservation is a guaranteed content-level behavior, not a styling choice that silently breaks if CSS fails to load.
accessibility_effect: Screen readers can read preserved line breaks and spacing; pairing pre with code clarifies that the content is source code rather than prose.
seo_effect: No independent ranking effect; correctly marked-up code samples stay crawlable as real text instead of being rendered only through CSS or canvas tricks.
constraints: Pair with code for source code; content inside is whitespace-significant.
